subject: Crestware inference evaluation — speed & cost playbook
messages:
From: Darren Cole <darren@crestware.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Ananya Patel <ananya.patel@crestware.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Crestware inference evaluation — performance & cost

Thanks for the call earlier, Laura — good to meet the team. Quick recap from our side and where we need to narrow scope before a perf run:

- Target UX: chat-like assistant with short queries (avg 40 tokens in, 40 tokens out) and a secondary long-form summarization path (streaming; avg 1k output tokens).
- P95 target for chat path: <= 150ms (US region), goal P99 < 300ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 350 QPS for chat path during business hours, bursts to 2k QPS for 90s during peak events.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~200 active users, but we need headroom for spikes; planning for concurrency 1k.
- Streaming needs: initial token latency <= 200ms and sustained token rate >= 25 tokens/s.
- Budget: looking to optimize cost; internal procurement expects a clear per-1k-token estimate.

I'll attach sample payloads and a rough traffic shape. We want Redwood's recommendation for configuration and an estimate of unit cost for both hosted and dedicated options. Also need to understand fallback behavior (model variant, caching) if capacity is constrained.

Thanks,
Darren
Head of ML Engineering
Crestware
(attachment: crestware_sample_payloads.json)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Darren Cole <darren@crestware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestware inference evaluation — performance & cost

Darren — thanks for the clear recap and the sample payloads. Notes and proposals from Redwood below. Summary first, details after.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Start with a targeted perf run on hosted with a canary directed traffic approach: 5% of traffic routed to a low-latency config using a quantized model variant + continuous batching + prefix KV caching.
- Primary levers: continuous batching (reduce per-token cost at steady state), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and an int8 quantization profile for chat path. For streaming long-form, use the full-precision variant with concurrent request sharding.
- Expected delta: ~30-45% token-cost reduction on chat path with quantization + batching + caching; streaming path will prioritize latency over max quantization to keep generation quality.

Details / questions we need from Crestware to finalize the perf plan:
1) Confirm representative sample of 1000 requests for chat and 200 for long-form (we got the attached but please mark which are canonical).
2) Provide a 24-hr traffic shape CSV (we can accept the simple summary you already attached).
3) Any hard SLAs required for P99 (you mentioned goal <300ms — is that a must or a target?).

Planned perf-run configuration and rationale:
- Chat path (short queries): use quantized 8-bit model variant (we call this q8-dynamic) + continuous batching tuned for 40–80 token seq lengths; target batch size window 40–120ms depending on arrival rate. This keeps P95 ~120–150ms in our previous benchmarks for similar payloads.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for common system/user prompts; expect cache hit rates 10–30% saving tokens and reducing tail latency.
- Streaming: route long-form to a full-precision variant and use pipeline prefetching of KV state. Streaming concurrency per GPU tuned to 8–12 simultaneous streams to keep token emission latency low.
- Fallback policy: if quantized pool is saturated, route to the compatible full-precision variant (slower/higher cost) or degrade to a shorter context-based response. We can set an automatic fallback threshold (e.g., CPU/GPU queue > 70%).

Attachments: redwood_performance-playbook.pdf (short playbook), bench-plan-crestware.md (initial test plan).

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm samples + traffic shape (by EOD Thu).
- We schedule a 2-hour perf run window next Tue (Redwood engineers + Crestware infra contact).
- Post-run: Redwood provides a one-page cost/latency tradeoff brief and an ops runbook for the chosen config.

I'll loop Marissa for the bench specifics and Ben for cost math.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
(attachments: redwood_performance-playbook.pdf, bench-plan-crestware.md)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Darren Cole <darren@crestware.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Crestware inference evaluation — performance & cost

Darren — quick technical follow-up with the bench plan and expected numbers so you can share with infra/procurement: 

Bench plan highlights:
- Canary approach: 5% traffic on hosted; if results are good, move to 20% then 100% via rolling canary.
- Metrics we'll measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, cost-per-1k-tokens on the test config, cache-hit rate, batch size distribution, and quality regressions (sampling-based).

Initial sizing (empirical estimates for chat path):
- On a 40-token average seq, one A100-class GPU with q8-dynamic + continuous batching supports ~2.8k steady-state QPS with batching windows tuned; with streaming disabled. Real-world headroom for variability suggests we size 1 GPU per ~2k QPS for production resilience.
- For long-form streaming (1k-token outputs), expected per-GPU concurrency 8 streams and sustained emission 25–30 tokens/s; plan ~12–16 streams per GPU depending on token complexity.

Cost heuristics (hosted):
- Baseline (no quantization, no caching): $X.XX per 1k tokens.
- With q8-dynamic + batching + 20% cache hits: ~35% lower unit cost. Precise numbers after the perf run — Ben will provide a range.

Operational asks for the perf window:
- Send a low-priv network test user (we need a tenant id and an API key with test scope).
- Provide an account admin who can temporarily route 5% of traffic or provide traffic replay.

I'll run the bench scripts and capture a short-narrative ops report. Ben — can you prepare a draft cost table for hosted vs. dedicated with the above assumptions by EOD?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood
